tags.gist: Calls the two axes a reasonable heuristic but wants reversibility and time to consequence added, since slow, auditable, appealable paths differ from triage.
Wants a finer distinction within supervision, crediting independent determination before comparison more than a glance at a generated summary.
Wants traceability to a source artifact the reviewer can see, such as a photo or recording, as its own risk dimension.
Proposes a third category of user, trained and supervised non-clinical health workers, who fit neither the patient nor the professional label.
Wants risk assessment to weigh the supervisory structure around a user, not only whether the individual holds a license.
Wants the communication and comprehension element tested specifically for coordinators, for whom physician-level and consumer-level text both fail.
Argues omitting the non-clinical worker tier would also omit the homebound, low-literacy and non-English-speaking members they serve.
Wants routing a finding to an accountable care team recognized as a third option beyond escalate or not, with a different error profile.
Doubts any single error ratio generalizes; wants sponsors to state and justify their chosen ratio and report both rates separately.
Finds the range of confirmation approaches sound and agrees that a prospective study need not be demanded in every case.
Describes its own blinded adjudication: an independent reviewer records the correct finding from raw home inputs before seeing any output.
Wants adjudicator qualification defined by the task, since nurse assessors rather than physicians hold the standard for functional scoring.
Wants submissions to state whether the reference determination preceded seeing the output, and unblinded review not treated as equal to blinded.
Suggests blinded paired adjudication, feasible for small companies, be defined further as a confirmation method, perhaps through the MDDT program.
Says a clinician panel presumes a stable reference standard that Medicaid functional assessment lacks, with over 124 instruments and plan-specific scoring.
Notes field inter-rater agreement is largely unmeasured and wants sponsors to demonstrate, not assume, that a human reference standard exists.
Wants inter-rater agreement within the reference panel reported beside system-to-panel agreement, with each reviewer's instrument stated.
Wants consistency across assessors measurable as an endpoint in its own right where a function aims to reduce variance.
Strongly supports comparing against the existing alternative and thinks the paper should give that comparison greater weight.
Says the real alternative in home assessment is a rushed, often incomplete and unstandardized paper form, citing improper-payment data on missing documentation.
Notes unstandardized assessment produces duplication and gaps in equipment delivery, an outcome an idealized standard of care would not surface.
Wants sponsors allowed to document how care is actually delivered in the deployment setting and evaluate against that alongside any clinical reference.
Proposes health plans supply monitoring samples and outcome linkage under contract, while the manufacturer sets the specification and stays responsible.
